title: Reading Inflectional Endings
keyIdea: To read a long word, find the root first and then add the ending: jump + ing, cold + est, box + es, and un + lock + ed for a word with a part at the front too. Split at the root, not where the sounds seem to break (cold + est, not col + dest). Some endings add a beat: -es (box-es), and -ed after a root that ends in t or d (want-ed, land-ed); after other sounds -ed adds only a t or d sound (jumpt, playd). A double letter before the ending means the root has a short vowel (hopping from hop), and one letter can mean the root lost an e (hoping from hope). Cover the ending to check: if no word you know is left, it is not an ending (king, sister).
familyTip: Pick a word with an ending from a book page. Put your finger over the ending so only the root shows, read the root together, then lift your finger and read the whole word. Clap it: does the ending add a beat? Try hopping and hoping side by side and ask which one a rabbit does.

visual.caption: Does the ending add a beat? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: find where the ending starts, drum the beats, find the root of doubled words, sort look-alikes, and spot endings in sentences.

kid: A long word is often a root with an ending on the back. Cover the ending with your finger. Read the root. Then add the ending: jump, jumping.
Some endings add a beat. Clap box, then boxes: box-es. ed adds a beat only when the root ends in t or d: want-ed, land-ed. jumped has one beat. It sounds like jumpt.
Look for a double letter. hopping has two p's, so it comes from hop. hoping has one p, so it comes from hope. The e dropped off.
Not every word that ends in ing or er has an ending. Cover ing in king: k is not a word. So king is just king.
adult: Ages 5 to 7. The National Curriculum in England (Year 1 word reading) asks children to read words containing taught GPCs and -s, -es, -ing, -ed, -er and -est endings, and other words of more than one syllable. Year 2 adds reading and spelling words where the root changes: doubling the consonant after a short vowel (hopping, patted) and dropping e (hoping, liked). In the US this is Common Core RF.1.3f and RF.1.3g (read two-syllable words, read inflectional endings) and RF.2.3d (common prefixes and suffixes).

The terms: the root (base word) carries the meaning and an inflectional ending (an inflection, or inflectional suffix) adds number, tense or comparison without changing the word class. The past tense -ed has three pronunciations: /ɪd/ after t or d (wanted, landed), /t/ after other voiceless sounds (jumped, looked) and /d/ after voiced sounds (played, hugged). Plural -es is /ɪz/ after s, x, z, sh and ch, so it adds a syllable; plain -s does not.

Common mistakes: splitting by syllable instead of by root (col-dest, jum-ping), saying jump-ed with an extra beat, reading every final ing or er as an ending (king, sister, letter), and reading hoping as hopping because the root e is gone. The fix is the same each time: cover the ending and check that a real root is left.

In the lab your child taps the first letter of the ending in six words, taps a drum once for each beat in seven words, picks the root of seven doubled or e-dropped words (hopping, hoping, tapping, taped), sorts eight words into a real ending or just ends that way, and taps every word with an ending in four sentences, including traps like sister and king.

practice.prompt: What is the root in jumping?
practice.hint: Cover ing. What word is left?
practice.explain: Cover ing and jump is left, a word you know. jum-ping splits by sound, not by root.

practice.prompt: A root has {n} letters and does not change when you add ing, like jump and jumping. How many letters does the new word have?
practice.hint: ing has three letters, and the root keeps all of its letters.
practice.explain: {n} letters in the root plus 3 for ing gives {=n+3}. jump has 4 and jumping has 7.

practice.prompt: How many beats does landed have?
practice.hint: Does land end in t or d? Then ed adds a beat.
practice.explain: land ends in d, so ed adds a beat: land-ed has two beats.

practice.prompt: You read {a} words ending in ed. {b} of them have a root ending in t or d, like wanted. How many of the words have just one beat, like jumped?
practice.hint: Only roots ending in t or d get an extra beat from ed.
practice.explain: {b} words get the extra beat, so {a} − {b} = {=a-b} words have one beat, like jumped.

practice.prompt: What is the root in hoping?
practice.hint: Is there one p or two before the ending?
practice.explain: hoping has one p, so the root lost its e: hope. hop would make hopping, with two p's.

pool.prompt: Which word has a real ending added?
pool.hint: Cover er. Is a word you know left?
pool.explain: Cover er in taller and tall is left. sist and lett are not words, so sister and letter just end in er.

pool.hint: Two n's before ing mean a short vowel.
pool.explain: The n was doubled before ing, so the root is run, with a short u.

pool.prompt: How many beats does jumped have?
pool.hint: jump does not end in t or d.
pool.explain: jumped sounds like jumpt. ed adds a t sound, not a beat, so it has one beat.

pool.prompt: How do you split coldest to read it?
pool.hint: Find the root first, then the ending after it.
pool.explain: Cover est and cold is left. Read the root, then the ending: cold + est.

pool.prompt: Which word has an ending that adds a beat?
pool.hint: Clap each word. Listen for an extra beat at the end.
pool.explain: wish ends in sh, so es adds a beat: wish-es. cats and helps have one beat.

pool.prompt: Read the word unlocked. Which chunks are in it?
pool.hint: Find the root in the middle, then the parts on each side.
pool.explain: lock is the root, un is at the front and ed is at the end: un + lock + ed.

pool.prompt: A root has {n} letters and ends in a short vowel and one letter, like hop. You double the last letter and add ing. How many letters now?
pool.hint: One extra letter for the double, three for ing.
pool.explain: {n} letters, plus 1 for the doubled letter, plus 3 for ing, gives {=n+4}. hop has 3 and hopping has 7.

pool.prompt: A sentence has {a} words. {b} of them have an ending added. How many words have no ending?
pool.hint: Take the words with endings away from all the words.
pool.explain: {a} words take away the {b} with endings leaves {=a-b} without an ending.

pool.prompt: Which word is a root on its own, with no ending?
pool.hint: Cover ing in each one. Is a word you know left?
pool.explain: Cover ing in king and only k is left, so king has no ending. singing is sing + ing, and rings is ring + s.
